This appears to be a CBP ruling on retractable screens made of PVC-coated fiberglass mesh. The likely classification is 7019 (glass fibers and articles thereof) or 3925 (builders' ware of plastics), or possibly 6303 (curtains, blinds) or 5603.

The fabric is PVC-coated fiberglass woven mesh, which would fall in 7019.59 (other woven fabrics) or 7019.90. But the finished article is a retractable screen, an assembly with a roller and rails. The candidates are:
- 7019.90 (other articles of glass fibers).
- 3925.30 (shutters, blinds, including Venetian blinds, and similar articles and parts thereof). This is plastics-based, but the fabric is coated glass fiber.
- 6303 (curtains, including drapes, and interior blinds). 6303.19 covers other materials, but glass fiber textile is in Section XI, and 6303.12 covers synthetic fibers. Glass fibers are textile materials in Section XI, so 6303.92 (of synthetic fibers, knitted) and 6303.19 (of other textile materials) are possible. It is an exterior screen, not interior, so 6303 is less likely.
- 6307.90 (other made-up articles).

I recall rulings on Phantom or similar retractable screens that went to 7019.90.9000 or 6303.99. Another possibility is 7019.59 with the woven glass fabric. For a retractable screen assembly of PVC-coated fiberglass mesh, I believe the ruling classified it under 7019.90.9000, "Other articles of glass fibers," since the fabric gives the essential character. Since the fabric is a made-up item, 7019.90 is the best fit. The 10-digit code is 7019.90.9000.
